title: Initial Spread of the SarsCov2 Virus: Analysis of the First Contacts Clusters in the City of Luanda
content: (1) Background: After the occurrence of the first Covid19 case on February 21, 2020 in Angola, prevention actions were intensified. Active contacts’ tracing was assumed to be the most important and efficient measure to control the spreading of the disease in the capital city Luanda. (2) Methods: An observational descriptive study was carried out on 53 contacts traced by active research teams, and demographic, symptoms, occurrence days and diagnosis variables were evaluated. Cluster analysis was made using SPSS dendrograms and Excel graphic radar models. (3) Results: Contacts have been generated by two index suspected cases registered as number 026 and 031 not previously tested, that violated isolation measures. Index case 026, generated 23 contacts being 12 men (52.2%) and 11 women (47.8%), while index case 031 generated 30 contacts 16 men (53.3%) and 14 women (46.7%). (4) Conclusions: Contacts’ cluster analysis showed that their hierarchical distribution and sequential progression had a family relationship for index case 026, and an immigrant commercial relationship for the index case 031. Emphasis must be given to contact tracing teams as well as families and immigrants in further outbreaks.
